game: SF @ ATL Week 7 2026 / kickoff time not in pack / ATL +2.5 / total 50 / weather not saved

script.base: Books have SF -2.5 with a 50 total, implied ATL 23.8 and SF 26.2, so a close high-play game rather than a blowout or a slog. Atlanta can keep feeding Bijan Robinson (45 carries, 292 yards over weeks 4-6) with Brian Robinson out, while still throwing to Drake London and Kyle Pitts. San Francisco, without Mike Evans (23 targets, 396 air yards) and Deebo Samuel, leans on Christian McCaffrey on the ground and George Kittle in the short and middle game, with Brock Purdy not needing to win a shootout.
script.flip1: SF jumps ahead by two scores. Atlanta abandons Bijan, London and Pitts targets spike, and McCaffrey's rush line dies while his receiving work may rise. Starters are not at true blowout rest risk on a 2.5 spread unless this flip actually happens.
script.flip2: Atlanta controls the clock with Bijan (and the extra carries from Brian Robinson being out). SF's thinned receiver room cannot throw them back into it, the game gets run-heavier than a 50 total implies, and Pitts and London unders become live while McCaffrey carries stay viable only if SF is not trailing.

injury_fallout: SF WR Mike Evans is out (ribs) and WR Deebo Samuel Sr. is out (hamstring), so 23+9 targets and Deebo's 5 carries / 48 rush yards from the last three games have to move. Next men: George Kittle already has 20 targets / 163 yards, McCaffrey 18 targets / 86 yards and 42 carries, with Brandin Cooks (5 targets / 20 yards), Kyle Juszczyk (4/38), Jacob Cowing (3/9) and Jordan Watkins (last4 receiving yards 60, 22) fighting for the rest. Christian Kirk is questionable (calf) and has no prior games on the card, so he is not a counted absorber. SF DE Nick Bosa is out (knee), S Marques Sigle is out (ankle), CB Upton Stout and S Siran Neal are questionable, and LBs Luke Gifford and Garret Wallow are out: Atlanta's pass catchers, especially the tight end, face a thinner pressure and second-level unit. ATL RB Brian Robinson is out (hamstring; 23 carries / 79 yards and 4 targets in three games), so Bijan is the only healthy lead back. ATL WR Beaux Collins is out and Olamide Zaccheaus is questionable (shoulder; last4 3, 9, 0, 0), which tightens Atlanta targets onto London, Pitts and Jahan Dotson. ATL LB Divine Deablo is out (forearm), which helps Kittle and McCaffrey as receivers. ATL DEs Za'Darius Smith and Samson Ebukam and DT Gervon Dexter Sr. are questionable; if the edges sit, Purdy sees less pressure. Sources: pack injury report and weeks 4-6 target/carry logs. Final inactives are not in the pack.

pre_mortem: It's Monday and both legs lost. Atlanta rode Bijan — 45 carries and 292 yards in the prior three weeks, with Brian Robinson out adding more — and Penix's dropback EPA (0.00 vs blitz, -0.28 otherwise) never supported a second weapon, so Pitts repeated the 5-yard dud under 34.5. McCaffrey finished at 52 or worse because Atlanta's 3.83 YPC front is not a give, Keaton Black took another chunk of the 20 carries he has been getting, and a second-half deficit turned the 49ers into a Kittle dropback game. The coin-flip -114/-115 prices were the tell that the injuries were already in the number. Weather is not saved, so a wind or rain cut to volume was never checked. That counter is real on McCaffrey, which is why he is a lean; it is not stronger than the Pitts read, because 34.5 only needs a few catches and the linebackers are actually out.
slip_story: One competitive-game story, not a shootout stack and not a total-under mix: SF 26.2 / ATL 23.8, both teams using the weapon the injuries left them. Pitts over is the Atlanta pass leg against missing SF linebackers; McCaffrey rush over is the SF run leg after Evans and Deebo. They can hit together if the game stays within a score. They fail together only in a slog. London was the tighter Atlanta stack partner and was left off (see data_check). No touchdown legs, one market per player, no depth-receiver adds (Watkins, Cooks, Herbert, Kirk).
